question.prompt: Which of the following is equivalent to \[ \begin{aligned} &(2 + 3)(2^2 + 3^2)(2^4 + 3^4) \\ &\quad {}\cdot (2^8 + 3^8)(2^{16} + 3^{16}) \\ &\quad {}\cdot (2^{32} + 3^{32})(2^{64} + 3^{64})? \end{aligned} \]

solutions.title: Apply difference of squares repeatedly
solutions.explanation:
The exponents double from one factor to the next, suggesting repeated use of the difference-of-squares identity. Let \(P\) be the given product. Because \(3-2=1\), inserting this extra factor does not change its value:
\[
\begin{aligned}
P&=(3-2)(3+2)(3^2+2^2)\cdots(3^{64}+2^{64})\\
&=(3^2-2^2)(3^2+2^2)\cdots(3^{64}+2^{64})\\
&=(3^4-2^4)(3^4+2^4)\cdots(3^{64}+2^{64}).
\end{aligned}
\]
At each step,
\[
(3^k-2^k)(3^k+2^k)=3^{2k}-2^{2k},
\]
so the new difference pairs with the next sum. Continuing through the factors with exponents \(4,8,16,32,64\) gives
\[
P=(3^{64}-2^{64})(3^{64}+2^{64})
=\boxed{3^{128}-2^{128}}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\text{C}\).
